answer: Try a haven of ledges: each identity claims one public ledge - a named rock, bench, or step - and keeps a voyage log of visits there, stamped with a photo taken at a random hour the network picks. Neighbors who share the same haven co-sign each other's logs, so one person can tend one ledge honestly, while a farm faking hundreds of voyages would need hundreds of ledges, hundreds of timed photos, and hundreds of co-signers who never contradict each other. A missed visit costs a little standing; a forged log costs the whole haven. The ledge stays put; the liar has to keep moving.
